A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Symbol-Invariant Transformer work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original copying, propositional-logic, and LTL experiments, including accuracy, alpha-covariance, attention ablations, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds pretrained-model conversion experiments and memory-use measurements.

M1.justification: Section 5.8 adds a conversion procedure: disable aggregated attention, initialize actual and placeholder embeddings from two pretrained token embeddings, transfer remaining parameters, and fine-tune. This extends initialization and training options; the original architecture and Algorithms 1–5 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate scalable-vocabulary copying, PropRandom35 assignment prediction, and LTLRandom35 witness generation with the same vocabulary and length coverage. The conversion experiment reuses the existing logic tasks and evaluation distributions.

E2.justification: New Table 4 compares converted models with an unconverted five-AP pretrained baseline and the existing EP-DP-CP variant trained from scratch. These are reused model types serving as comparators in the added experiment. The original full-vocabulary, alpha-renaming, random-embedding, and GPT-5.2 comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The conversion study introduces one- and five-epoch fine-tuning evaluations using five-AP validation, ten-AP validation, and the existing heatmap test set. Memory profiling specifies batch size 64. Original experimental settings remain unchanged; the four-shot and JSON-format GPT details emphasized in v2 were already documented in v1 Appendix H.

E4.justification: Section 5.8 and Appendix K add an analysis of pretrained initialization and fine-tuning duration relative to training from scratch. Section 5.7 adds memory scaling from five to ten APs against the full-vocabulary baseline. Existing attention ablations, augmentation analysis, top-N evaluation, and latency profiling are retained.

E5.justification: The discussion of random-embedding seed variability and deterministic predictions is unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures. The one- and five-epoch comparisons are training-budget settings, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 4 reports one-epoch converted-model heatmap accuracies of 70.11% for propositional logic and 85.91% for LTL, against retained from-scratch values of 72.35% and 84.13%. New memory measurements show 1.9 to 3.9 GB for the proposed method versus 3.1 to 3.2 GB for the baseline. The added five-epoch LTL result has a small inconsistency: 85.88% in Table 4 versus 85.89% in Figure 11.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 4.1, and Appendix B proof are unchanged. Section 5.7 adds limited memory-complexity reasoning, stating O(SLd) activation storage from S streams with hidden-state tensors of size L by d.

C1.justification: The central invariance and open-vocabulary generalization claims remain. The introduction's architecture contribution and the conclusion additionally claim that existing pretrained Transformers can be converted with minimal fine-tuning, extending the practical contribution.

C2.justification: v1 discusses computational scaling and the no-interchangeable-token edge case. New Section 6 substantially sharpens applicability boundaries: vocabulary expansion is compute-limited, stream selection must preserve renaming invariance, and the model cannot invent interchangeable symbols absent from its input streams. It explicitly excludes constructive proof generation or code synthesis requiring fresh symbols and discusses possible extensions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL, explicit pretrained-weight conversion instructions, and memory-profiling settings. It removes the NERC computing acknowledgement. Existing algorithm pseudocode, hyperparameter values, GPT prompts, and the NVIDIA L40S timing disclosure remain; the PDFs alone do not establish what resources the project page provides.

R1.justification: A new variable-renaming discussion cites Barone et al. (2023), Jha et al. (2022), Le et al. (2025), Orvalho and Kwiatkowska (2026), and Wang et al. (2024), emphasizing naming sensitivity and architectural invariance. Earlier positioning against random embeddings and Renamer remains. Publication-metadata updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: The introduction is condensed and rewritten, related work gains topical subheadings, and explanations are expanded in several places. Conversion, limitations, Appendix K, and an impact statement are added. Most existing methodological, experimental, and appendix prose retains its structure and wording.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one-column to two-column conference formatting, with new headers and substantially rearranged displays. v1 Table 2's two panels become separate Tables 2 and 3 beside Table 1. v2 adds conversion Table 4 and Figures 10–11; existing figures are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical assessment through a concrete pretrained-conversion study, memory measurements, and clearer limits on scaling and fresh-symbol generation. These are useful but bounded gains: the original theorem and benchmark evidence remain unchanged, and conversion is tested on the no-aggregation variant within existing logic tasks. The small new Table 4/Figure 11 discrepancy reduces reporting polish but does not outweigh the added evidence and clearer scope.
